sources.entry: roampal-core by roampal-ai - Outcome-based persistent memory MCP server for Claude Code and OpenCode. Good advice promoted, bad advice demoted. pip install roampal.

summary.one_liner: roampal-core is an outcome-based persistent memory MCP server for Claude Code and OpenCode that injects relevant past context into each prompt and promotes or demotes memories based on whether the advice worked.
summary.what_it_does: Roampal runs a local HTTP server (port 27182) that Claude Code hooks and the OpenCode plugin call before each user message to inject relevant memories into the prompt. Memories are stored in five collections (working, history, patterns, memory_bank, books) with promotion, demotion and expiry rules. After each exchange the outcome is scored: in Claude Code the main LLM calls a score_memories tool, while in OpenCode an independent sidecar model scores the exchange. Storage uses ChromaDB with multilingual embeddings and a cross-encoder reranker, all running on CPU via ONNX Runtime. Named memory profiles and directory bindings keep separate memory stores per project or client. The CLI covers setup, server control, stats, diagnostics, book ingestion, and sidecar configuration.
use_cases: give Claude Code memory of past fixes and preferences across sessions
keep separate memory stores for different projects
stop an AI coding assistant repeating previously rejected advice
store personal preferences the assistant should always follow
ingest reference documents for the AI to search
run a fully local memory layer for coding agents
notable: Outcome scoring: good advice is promoted and bad advice demoted, rather than just storing everything
OpenCode scoring uses an independent sidecar model so the main assistant never grades its own answers
Five memory collections with lifetimes from 24 hours to permanent
Named memory profiles with per-directory binding and a per-request profile header
Runs fully on CPU with no GPU; models download automatically on first use
caveats: Needs about 500MB RAM and roughly 500MB of disk for models
Only Claude Code and OpenCode are supported; Claude Code has no independent scorer and relies on the main LLM for scoring
OpenCode scoring is off until the user explicitly configures a scoring model; Zen free models send data to opencode.ai and may be logged
Developed primarily on Windows; macOS and Python 3.13 are CI-tested as of v0.6.0
